day_channel.message: With only three of us left, we really need to re-examine everyone's claims before we commit to a vote. Player_9 and Player_10, let's hear how you reconcile the remaining roles on board.

Player_10 has verified their sentinel role through consistent night records, and I am the investigator. That leaves Player_7 as the necromancer holding the final threat against us, since all other town roles are accounted for.

If you are both so certain town is fully accounted for, why did your investigation on player_6 only happen after the wagon was already moving? It is awfully convenient how your results always magically match whatever narrative player_10 is pushing.

I checked player_6 on night two because their trailseer claim fell apart under scrutiny. Catching an illusionist isn't some magical coordination with player_10, it is simply an investigative result coming to light right when the town needed to see the truth.

You two have locked arms so tightly that neither of you ever has to prove anything independently. If Player_10 was really watching everything, why didn't they catch who was interfering earlier instead of just echoing Player_9's late investigations? One of you is deflecting to secure a safe endgame.

Player_10's watches mapped out actual night visits on earlier rounds while you abstained and deflected, player_7. Your desperate attempts to drive a wedge between us only highlight that you are the last threat standing as the necromancer.

My watches weren't just echoing anything, player_7; night one caught the exact visits by the dead wolves player_5 and player_6 at player_4's door. Player_9's check on player_6 just lined up with the visits I tracked. You are deflecting because my hard tracking backs up the investigator instead of your evasions.

Player_10 claims your watches caught the wolves, yet you never once questioned why player_9's checks magically appeared right when a bandwagon needed justification. If your tracking is so bulletproof, why did you only corroborate each other after the votes were already locked in?

My watch on player_6 on night two caught player_9 visiting them, which directly confirms their investigator check on the illusionist. You keep calling it coordination because you are scrambling to hide the fact that you are the necromancer.

Player_10, saying your watch on night two caught player_9 visiting player_6 is awfully convenient mutual backing when both your claims depend entirely on each other. If you two weren't coordinating, one of you would have verifiable town results that didn't magically interlock only when challenged.
Before the vote: player_7 has been accused by player_9 and player_10. player_7 gets a last word.

If you both assume my guilt solely because your claims interlock, you are ignoring how easily two players can construct a closed narrative together. Neither of you has produced a result that wasn't immediately validated by the other's convenient timing. Look closely at how your stories rely entirely on each other before casting a blind vote.
